newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks lose ground in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks lose ground in quiet trade.

text.p: Shares on the Jordan stock exchange fell 0.37 percent in quiet trade on Sunday, surrendering recent gains as blue-chip stocks went into decline.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.55 points to 146.69 points in trade worth 424,000 dinars ($565,000).
Falling shares outnumbered gainers by 23 to five and the half dozen busiest shares on the bourse all lost ground. But brokers said they did not expect a sustained tumble.
"The market's just quiet. It's not going up and it's not going down," said Nasser al-Amad, general manager of United Financial Investment.

The exchange, worried that trade to the West Bank and sanction-hit Baghdad remains blocked, has been trapped one point either side of 147.7 for the last two months. Turnover has halved to around 500,000 dinars a day.

Sunday's trade was again dominated by Jordan Gulf Bank, with turnover of 121,000 dinars. The stock fell 0.01 dinars to 0.94 dinars. Investors had been buying Jordan Gulf shares on the back of rumours of strong earnings in 1996.
International Tobacco, producer of the only locally made "light" cigarettes, lost some of its recent gains, slipping 0.01 to 1.16 dinars in busy trade.
Popular stocks Livestock and Poultry and Arab Bank were other high-profile losers on Sunday.
"Livestock and Poultry has been going up and down for months," said Amad. "Speculators have found it an easy share to push around -- they attract the investors and then pull their legs."
